minutes.headline: Board agreed to send a resident's repeated complaints back to the board, denied a police audit, ratified a facilities head.
minutes.summary: Short, weather-shortened meeting. The board discussed guidance to the town manager on one resident's high-volume complaints and rejected his request for a police financial audit. It ratified the facilities superintendent, approved a Class 2 auto dealer license and opened the town meeting warrant. A member reported the school committee is weighing position cuts for the coming school budget.

public_comment.topic: Asked whether the health insurance stabilization line item still exists and how much is in it; the town manager said about 101,000 remains.

votes.motion: Ratify the town manager's appointment of Don gagy as facility superintendent.
Approve the Class 2 auto dealer license for Baker Enterprises (Auto Barn, 53 Chase Road).
Open the annual town meeting warrant January 9 and close it March 18, 2024 at 4 p.m.

budget_items.what_was_said: The school committee asked for guidance on electricity costs for next year's budget. The town manager said rates will go out to bid in spring and increases are expected after three years of a good locked rate.
An accounts payable warrant was presented.
Health insurance is expected to rise, with the exact number known late February or early March.
The superintendent presented a worst-case scenario of cutting positions across schools and central office.
The superintendent estimated ESSER loss accounts for some of the positions.
The state made mid-year 9C cuts; Lunenburg appears unscathed because the cuts were limited to earmarks and agency budgets.
A portion was used this year; a small cushion remains.

decisions.decision: Board gave the town manager guidance to keep responses to the resident brief and to offer that he appear before the board; the invitation to meet stands.
Request for a financial audit of the police department was denied; no member wanted to pursue it.
Town manager goals update pushed to next week; ARPA update and draft board committee handbook also set for next week.

what_happened.line: The Select Board denied a request for a financial audit of the police department; no member wanted to pursue it.
The board gave the town manager guidance to keep replies to one resident's repeated complaints brief and to invite him to appear before the board.
The board ratified the town manager's appointment of a facilities superintendent and approved a Class 2 auto dealer license, 4-0 by roll call.
The board opened the annual town meeting warrant on January 9 and set it to close March 18, 2024 at 4 p.m., 4-0 by roll call.
A member reported the superintendent presented a worst-case scenario of cutting school and central office positions, partly tied to the end of ESSER money.

why_it_matters: The school position cuts, a health insurance increase still to be set, and electricity rates going to bid in spring are early pressures on the budgets residents will vote on at town meeting.
The warrant closes March 18, 2024, which is the deadline for articles to be placed before voters at the annual town meeting.
watch_next: The town meeting warrant closes March 18, 2024 at 4 p.m.
Next week's board agenda: town manager goals update, ARPA update and the draft board committee handbook.
